then.text: Saggars all good? Course they are. I knocked the bottoms out meself.
From the fireman at Gladstone? Then you'll be after saggars. You've come to the right man. The only man, these days.
A saggar's a fireclay box. The ware goes inside, safe from smoke and flame. I'm the bottom knocker: I beat out the clay for the base, flat and even, with a mallet in a metal ring.
Proper job title, that. People think it's a joke. It's on the census!
Here's a stack of good ones. Tell the fireman to mind the third from the top, it's got a temper.

else.text: Yes, that's my job. Yes, really. No, I don't want to hear your joke. I've heard it.

decorator.text: See this? Transfer printing. Ink a copper plate, print onto tissue, then rub the tissue onto the pot. The pattern stays when you peel it off.
Blue and white, a bit wobbly, every one slightly different. That's how you know a person made it.

engine_man.text: That's the steam engine. Drove the whole works, through belts and shafts, back in the day. We still fire it up on special days.
Boats used to tie up right outside to load crates for Liverpool and the world. The canal was the motorway, then.
